articles.title: Por que Fergie saiu dos Black Eyed Peas e quem canta com eles hoje?  | G1
articles.standfirst: Trio se apresenta no Rock in Rio no dia 6 de setembro. Entenda por que a cantora não faz parte do grupo, apesar de encontros recentes, e quem é a vocalista atual.
articles.summary: Trio se apresenta no Rock in Rio no dia 6 de setembro. Entenda por que a cantora não faz parte do grupo, apesar de encontros recentes, e quem é a vocalista atual.
articles.body:
Os Black Eyed Peas se apresentam no Rock in Rio no dia 6 de setembro, no Palco Mundo. Essa é a segunda vez do grupo no festival: eles vieram em 2019, em show com participação de Anitta.

Na época da última vinda, os Black Eyed Peas já eram um trio, sem a presença de Fergie. Mas até hoje, a cantora é lembrada por ter feito parte dos hits mais icônicos da banda. Abaixo, relembre por que Fergie saiu do grupo e quem é a atual vocalista feminina do Black Eyed Peas:

Por que Fergie saiu dos Black Eyed Peas?

Os Black Eyed Peas foram formados nos anos 90 como um trio. Fergie entrou no grupo em 2002, durante a produção do disco "Elephunk" e, a partir daí, o grupo atingiu seu auge comercial.

Com Fergie, discos como "Monkey Business", "The E.N.D." e "The Beginning" tiveram vários hits e colocaram o grupo no topo das paradas. Isso até 2011, quando o grupo anunciou que iria dar uma pausa por tempo indeterminado.

Os Black Eyed Peas voltaram em 2015, com singles lançados já sem a participação de Fergie. Até então, dizia-se que era só uma pausa para a vocalista focar no seu segundo álbum solo, "Double Dutchess".

Sua saída foi oficializada só em 2017, por Will.i.Am, que reforçou que a cantora não seria substituída . Segundo os integrantes, não foi um rompimento hostil.

Anos mais tarde, Taboo disse que, naquela época, Fergie saiu porque queria se dedicar integralmente à maternidade.

Recentemente, os quatro voltaram a aparecer juntos. Em uma entrevista com o produtor brasileiro Papatinho, veiculada em janeiro deste ano, Will.I.Am revelou que "o sonho dele" era fazer um disco do Black Eyed Peas para o Carnaval do Rio.

"Imagina se o Black Eyed Peas fizer um álbum sobre o Carnaval do Rio e no Carnaval do Rio. E sou eu, Taboo, Apl e Fergie. Isso seria épico. Se a gente fosse trazer essa formação de volta, isso precisa acontecer no Brasil, no Carnaval. Esse é o palco para isso", disse.

Em maio, o grupo foi como um quarteto para receber um prêmio nos American Music Awards. Apesar disso, não há confirmação de que ela vai voltar para o grupo.

Will.i.Am fez o possível para cumprir sua promessa de não substituir Fergie. Hoje, os Black Eyed Peas são oficialmente um trio, mas contam com a ajuda de vocais femininos para os maiores hits. Afinal, faixas como "Meet Me Halfway" ou "Boom Boom Pow" não seriam as mesmas sem os trechos da cantora.

Atualmente, quem costuma fazer essa parte é a cantora filipina J. Rey Soul .

J. Rey Soul é a atual cantora do Black Eyed Peas — Foto: Reprodução/Facebook

Às vezes, o grupo também convida cantores de algumas parcerias, como aconteceu com Anitta no Rock in Rio de 2019. Juntos, eles lançaram a canção "Explosion".

articles.title: Lionel Richie segue na UTI para investigar problema cardíaco | G1
articles.standfirst: Lionel Richie foi internado após passar mal no fim de uma apresentação em St. Louis. Cantor tem previsão de alta para quarta-feira (3).
articles.summary: Lionel Richie segue internado em uma UTI nos EUA para exames cardíacos após passar mal em show, com previsão de alta para esta quarta-feira (3).
articles.body:
Lionel Richie durante apresentação no show de coroação do Rei Charles III, em Londres, em 7 de maio de 2023 — Foto: Chris Jackson/Pool via Reuters

Lionel Richie, de 77 anos, segue internado na Unidade de Terapia Intensiva (UTI) após passar mal durante um show nos EUA. Segundo o site TMZ, o cantor passa por uma bateria de exames por conta de problemas cardíacos.

Segundo o TMZ, após dar entrada em um hospital local para realizar exames, os médicos investigam uma possível desidratação e a previsão era de alta nesta terça-feira (2).

No entanto, os médicos decidiram investigar como estava o coração do cantor. A previsão de alta foi alterada para esta quarta-feira (3).

Testemunhas que estavam no show relataram ao TMZ que Lionel aparentou ter dificuldades no fim da apresentação. Durante a última música, "All Night Long", ele pediu à equipe que levasse uma cadeira ao palco para que pudesse se sentar enquanto cantava.

Em junho, o cantor passou por outro susto. Após passar mal em um show na cidade de Saint Paul, ele foi levado às pressas para um hospital.

No dia, ele disse à plateia que estava "tonto" e "estranho".

Lionel Richie, nascido em 1949 no Alabama, é um dos maiores nomes do pop e do soul dos Estados Unidos. Ficou famoso nos anos 1970 como vocalista dos Commodores e depois seguiu carreira solo. Vendeu mais de 90 milhões de discos e ganhou quatro Grammys.

Entre os seus maiores hits estão "All Night Long (All Night)", "Hello" e "Say You, Say Me". Foi com esta última, tema do filme "O Sol da Meia-Noite", que Richie levou o Oscar de melhor canção original, em 1986. Ele também é jurado do programa "American Idol".

articles.title: Twenty One Pilots, eles cresceram: como dupla virou um dos maiores nomes do rock após três Lollas | G1
articles.standfirst: Banda encerra o Rock in Rio no dia 13 de setembro, no Palco Mundo. Baterista já explicou ao g1 por que é difícil perceber a própria evolução.
articles.summary: Banda encerra o Rock in Rio no dia 13 de setembro, no Palco Mundo. Baterista já explicou ao g1 por que é difícil perceber a própria evolução.
articles.body:
A trajetória do Twenty One Pilots no Brasil ajuda a entender não apenas a evolução técnica de Tyler Joseph e Josh Dun, mas como a próprio pop rock mudou nos últimos dez anos. A recusa de rótulos e o trânsito livre por estilos unem as maiores novidades recentes do rock.

Quando pisaram pela primeira vez no palco do Lollapalooza, em 2016, eles eram vistos por parte do público como uma curiosidade: uma dupla com pose de youtubers mascarados, mistura afiada de rap com indie e uma energia que compensava a escassez de instrumentos com o uso de bases pré-gravadas e acrobacias.

Twenty One Pilots se apresentam no palco Skol do Lollapalooza 2016 — Foto: Flavio Moraes/G1

Naquela estreia, faixas como "Stressed Out" e "Car Radio" já mostravam o apelo direto com a fatia mais jovem da plateia. Era um som moldado por dilemas existenciais, letras com tom positivo e uma salada de influências que ia do hip hop ao poperô. Em entrevista ao g1 na época , Josh Dun justificava a formação enxuta e a mistura estilística: "A gente notou que tocava melhor assim. Mas ao mesmo tempo, nos sentimos vulneráveis com só dois no palco". A vulnerabilidade virou combustível.

Três anos depois, no Lollapalooza 2019, o cenário era outro. A dupla desembarcou no Autódromo de Interlagos carregando a era "Trench", que pintou a plateia de preto e amarelo com fitas, lenços e cabelos tingidos . Maior, o duo foi eleito o melhor show daquela edição, entregando um caos sonoro e performático que reforçava a tese de "gênero fluido" defendida por Josh Dun antes de subir ao palco: "Não sei se o que tocamos é rock, e isso não importa".

A escalada do grupo não se restringiu às edições do festival paulistano. Em novembro de 2022, o Twenty One Pilots dividiu o protagonismo do GPWeek com o The Killers, tocando para 50 mil pessoas em São Paulo. No estádio do Palmeiras, Tyler e Josh provaram que já sabiam conduzir multidões. Ali começou a ficar evidente o amadurecimento musical, com arranjos mais dançantes (como o groove de "The Outside") e o apoio de uma banda no fundo, sem abrir mão do habitual show de luzes de celulares e da clássica escalada nas estruturas de iluminação.

Twenty One Pilots se apresenta no Lollapalooza 2023 — Foto: Rafael Leal/g1

A consagração em Interlagos veio em 2023, quando foram escalados de última hora para substituir o Blink-182. A dupla não estava sozinha em cena: baixista, tecladista, guitarrista e trompetista encorparam o som com R&B e disco music. O setlist ganhou até tributos brasileiros, como os versos de bossa nova e funk puxados pelos metais. Tyler manteve o ritual de escalar a estrutura de iluminação durante "Car Radio", mas o brilho veio nos arranjos que provaram o salto de patamar.

A caminhada iniciada lá em 2016 ganha um novo capítulo no dia 13 de setembro. Escalados para fechar o Rock in Rio, Tyler Joseph e Josh Dun chegam à Cidade do Rock não mais como uma aposta barulhenta ou uma aposta adolescente, mas como headliners consolidados. A dupla que começou se sentindo vulnerável com apenas dois integrantes no palco prova que a falta de fronteiras nos gêneros musicais foi o caminho mais direto para o topo do rock atual.

articles.title: Meet Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's new dog. She's already a model.
articles.summary: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s dog stepped into the spotlight with a starring role in Kelce’s new Tommy Hilfiger campaign.
articles.body:
There's a new addition to Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's family. The famous couple's white, fluffy Samoyed pup made her public debut in a new ad campaign.

The dog, rumored to be named Wendy, was first spotted earlier this summer when she stepped off a plane in Palm Springs with her Kansas City Chiefs tight end father and Grammy-winning mom. Alas, the world received no formal introduction to the pup — until Tuesday, when she appeared in a Tommy Hilfiger ad campaign alongside Kelce. The new ad shows Kelce checking into the Plaza Hotel with one very good girl by his side.

In an interview with Vogue about the campaign, which also features stars like Swift's bestie Gigi Hadid, Kelce said that their pup "lights up my day." So, naturally, when Tommy Hilfiger was seeking a dog to accompany Kelce in the campaign, the nepo puppy was the ideal choice.

"We figured, why not her? She crushed it and actually really fit into that Tommy aesthetic too," he told the magazine. "Those are some of my favorite shots."

The Samoyed may have been part of Kelce and Swift's lives for quite a while. In February 2025, Kelce's brother Jason Kelce revealed that the Happy Gilmore 2 actor had a new puppy — who ate the back of Kelce's velvet couch — on the Fitz & Whit podcast.

Swift, who wed Kelce at Madison Square Garden on July 3 after nearly three years of dating, has not had a dog of her own. The self-proclaimed "childless cat lady" has three cats — Olivia Benson, Meredith Grey and Benjamin Button — who often appear in her music videos and social media posts.

Despite being a cat person, Swift does have a dog sibling : Her mother Andrea Swift has a massive Great Dane — ironically named Kitty . In fact, Swift named a character in her song "The Life of a Showgirl" after Kitty .

articles.title: Ram Gopal Varma reacts to Allu Aravind's comment on Yash, says 'only highly egotistic people will take his statement personally', fans hit back at the 'Satya' maker
articles.summary: Filmmaker Ram Gopal Varma has stepped into the controversy surrounding producer Allu Aravind’s recent remark about Yash, coming to the latter’s defenc.
articles.body: Filmmaker Ram Gopal Varma has stepped into the controversy surrounding producer Allu Aravind’s recent remark about Yash, coming to the latter’s defence while arguing that the statement has been taken out of context.Allu Aravind had sparked a debate with his “Who was Yash before KGF?” comment. Reacting to the backlash, Varma described the controversy as “ridiculously laughable” and attempted to explain the context in which he believed the producer made the remark.Ram Gopal Varma wrote on X, “The controversy regarding #AlluAravind ‘s statement regarding #Yash is ridiculously laughable because what he clearly meant when he talked about big films with unknown actors and saying he dint know of Yash before KGF , even a dumbo should understand that it was in context of the below. The Hindi audience dint know Prabhas before Bahubali , they dint know Rishab before Kantara , I dint know Brando before Godfather..Maybe he was a star before in his films A street car named desire , on the water front etc ..I don’t know if they released in india also .. That’s because those films made them big stars and not the other way around ..Hollywood always spends big on concept films and not on stars ..Even directors like Nolan use names only for their acting prowess and not to depend on their stardom ..We all know whether it’s Oppenheimer or Odyssey , they would work as much irrespective of who’s in it."Varma argued that an actor’s popularity can change dramatically when a film reaches a much wider audience. Drawing parallels from Indian cinema, he pointed to Prabhas’ transformation into a pan-India star following Baahubali and Rishab Shetty’s increased recognition after Kantara. He also cited Hollywood icon Marlon Brando to illustrate how an actor can be established in one space but become significantly more recognised after appearing in a widely successful film.Varma then criticised those who interpreted Allu Aravind’s statement as a personal attack on Yash, suggesting that such reactions were driven by ego.“It’s only highly egotistic people who will take his statement personally on such a general well meaning thought ..Actually this kind of reaction also explains why they are making what they are making.”However, Varma’s intervention itself soon became a topic of discussion online. Some social media users interpreted his comments as another indirect dig at Yash rather than simply a defence of Allu Aravind.One user questioned, “You have been attacking Yash nonstop but he is not reacting to you, why?”Another asked, “Did Yash reject any of your scripts?”The exchange comes amid growing discussion around Yash’s journey from being a regional star to becoming a major pan-India name following the success of the KGF franchise.This statement also came amid the release of 'Toxic'. The film also stars Kiara Advani, Nayanthara, Huma Qureshi among others apart from Yash. Give your child the gift of confidence! Claim your exclusive TOI Masterclass spot today!

articles.title: Trump & Melania’s Marriage Reportedly ‘Not in a Healthy Place’ After Report She’s ‘Obsessed’ with His Aide—They ‘Barely Speak’
articles.summary: Will they ever work things out?
articles.body:
High-profile celebrity couples are frequently confronted with split rumors, and one pair that's faced such speculation for years is President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump .

Reports indicate they don't get along and even sleep in separate rooms, with new claims from The Irish Star suggesting that their marriage is barely hanging on by a thread.

According to the outlet, Trump's executive assistant, Natalie Harp , is partially to blame for the POTUS' strained relationship with Melania. Harp is reportedly "obsessed" with Trump and has been seen with him far more than Melania, who, according to The Daily Beast , has only been seen in public 38 days in 2026.

Trump biographer Michael Wolff previously alleged on his Substack that Melania's locked in a power struggle with Harp and "would not show up" to events if Harp was in attendance. Wolff also claimed that Trump and Melania "barely speak" these days.

In response, relationship expert Gemma Logan told The Irish Star that their marriage is likely "not in a healthy place."

"A marriage where two people are reportedly barely speaking is clearly not in a healthy place. Communication is the heartbeat of any long term relationship," she said. "When conversation becomes minimal, couples can start living parallel lives rather than a shared one. At that point, the question isn't simply whether they spend time together, but whether they still feel emotionally connected when they do."

Despite an alleged rough patch, Logan believes the two could eventually come back stronger than ever. "If reports about Donald and Melania Trump are accurate, the most important thing to remember is that distance in a marriage doesn't always mean the relationship is over."

"Some couples need constant closeness to feel connected," she continued. "Others function with far more independence, particularly when both partners have demanding lives, strong personalities and very different ways of dealing with public attention."

Logan even pointed out that there's a good chance a marriage "can survive distance"—as long as there isn't an "emotional disconnection" between both parties. "Living in different places doesn't automatically spell trouble. Plenty of couples have successful relationships while spending significant periods apart because of work, family responsibilities or lifestyle choices."

"The real issue is what happens emotionally during that time," she noted. "If the distance is mutually agreed, openly discussed and balanced with genuine affection, it can work. In some cases, a little breathing room can even make a relationship stronger."

Logan added, "However, if physical distance is being used to avoid conflict, emotional intimacy or difficult conversations, it can become a sign of a much deeper problem. The key question for Donald and Melania Trump is whether their separate routines are simply practical or whether they reflect a relationship that has become increasingly separate in every meaningful sense."

Even though Wolff alleged Melania has major issues with Harp, Hollywood insider Rob Shuter reported otherwise. Sources told Shuter that Melania is actually "relieved" that someone else is willing to be by Trump's side 24/7.

"Melania isn't jealous of Natalie — she's grateful for her," a Trumpworld source told Naughty But Nice . "Donald demands constant attention, and Natalie genuinely seems to enjoy giving it to him. For Melania, that takes an enormous amount of pressure off."

Another insider went on to say that Harp "wants to be there for every meeting, every trip, every moment," while Melania would rather skip it all. "They want entirely different relationships with Donald, and that's exactly why this works."

"Melania hates becoming part of somebody else's gossip, but she absolutely doesn't want Natalie gone," a separate source stated. "Why would she? Natalie handles the exhausting, around-the-clock Donald duty Melania has spent years avoiding."

articles.title: Dick Van Dyke shocks fans by posting inversion table workout at age 100
articles.summary: Dick Van Dyke, 100, shared a video of his inversion table workout on Instagram, proving his lifelong commitment to fitness is still going strong.
articles.body: When it comes to his fitness, Dick Van Dyke is not slowing down anytime soon. On Friday, Van Dyke, 100, shared a video of himself stretching on an inversion table. "#DVD100 1/2 workout inversion table #keepmoving," he captioned the clip, which he shared on Instagram on Friday, Aug. 28. ‘A MAN WITHOUT LOVE’ SINGER ENGELBERT HUMPERDINCK CREDITS UNDERWATER WORKOUT FOR KEEPING HIM ‘ALIVE’ AT 90 Fans took to the comments section to gush about the actor and his athletic skills. "I love this, let's all work out with DVD! We need you in this world and it makes me happy to see you!" one fan wrote, while another said: "Thank goodness you're doing amazing. Stay healthy." Other comments from fans include: "He's showing all of us what we could be doing. I'm not of course," "Stretching will definitely help you stay in your best shape," "Truly amazing and inspirational," "This is why you're going to outlive us all and I'm happy to be here for it." One fan said "Protect this man!!" while another simply wrote: "Very impressive!!!!" Last year, Van Dyke wrote an essay for The Times U.K., which described how staying active has been key to keeping himself physically strong and mentally sharp. "I still try to hit the gym three times a week," he explained. "I don’t know why this is something I still want to do, but it is. I’m not a ‘wake up and go back to bed’ type just yet, unless it’s cold and rainy. If I miss too many gym days, I really can feel it — a stiffness creeping in here and there. If I let that set in, well, God help me." WILLIAM SHATNER SAYS HE'S 'TAKING CARE OF BUSINESS' AT 95: 'THE LEAST OF ALL I WANT DO IS DIE' "At the gym, I usually do a circuit, going from one machine to the next without a break, in a circle," he said. "I start with the sit-up machine. Arlene says I could do 500, but that might be exaggerating. Then I do all the leg machines religiously, because my legs are two of my most cherished possessions. And then the upper body." "The secret ingredient is the music," he continued. "Most of my humming and singing really happens when I’m going from one machine to another. By ‘going’ I mean dancing. You heard me — dancing! And if I’m really feeling it, I’m no quiet warbler; I’m a Broadway belter." ELLEN BURSTYN ON THE HABITS SHE GAVE UP TO STAY THRIVING AT 93 YEARS OLD Van Dyke also gave up cigarettes and alcohol decades ago. And when he’s not breaking a sweat, Van Dyke makes it a priority to find something to be grateful for each day. "He wrote a couple of books ago about his hometown, Danville: ‘There’s a rich side of town, and there’s a poor side of town, but there’s not a bad side of town in Danville.’ I think he has a way to see that everything is great in life. articles.title: Luke Bryan threatens to 'knock the s--- out of' online trolls trashing his new song
articles.summary: Luke Bryan told Theo Von he'd confront trolls who accused his "Fish Hunt Golf Drink" song of being AI-generated, calling out teenage critics online.
articles.body: Luke Bryan has a bone to pick with his haters. During an appearance on the "This Past Weekend with Theo Von" podcast, the "American Idol" judge and country star opened up about the backlash surrounding his latest song, "Fish Hunt Golf Drink," which some social media users accused of being created with artificial intelligence. Bryan said the controversy began with a "narrative" created and amplified online. LUKE BRYAN CREDITS RELIGIOUS ROOTS AND SMALL-TOWN VALUES FOR HELPING HIM NAVIGATE A ‘CHALLENGING LIFE’ "That’s the crazy thing about where we’re at with social [media]," he said. "They started a narrative that we AI-ed it. And now, whether you like the song or not, or whether you like me as an artist, whether you like what I'm about or whatever … now I'm the guy that somebody said that I AI-ed a song and wrote it. "You get one or two kids with a bunch of Instagram, a bunch of followers, that say we AI-ed it, and then the whole world goes on their narrative." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS Von argued that he doesn't think people actually believe he used AI to create the song, but Bryan said the backlash has been "pretty crazy," and he recalled seeing posts from people who told him they hated him. "And they’re like at a camera going, ‘I hate you.’ … And I’m like, ‘I can see your face. If I see you one day, I’m going to f---ing knock the s--- out of you, dude,’" he said. However, Bryan acknowledged that many of the online comments were coming from teenagers. "And then I’m like, ‘Dude, you’re 16. You’re talking to a grown man who’s made a s--- ton of money doing this.' "It’s just so far out there," he added. "I’m like, if I caught my kids doing some stuff like that, I would kill them." Earlier this year, Bryan addressed the AI accusations shortly after the song's release. Some trolls kind of saying that I ‘AI-ed’ it, which is completely false," he told NBC4 at the Memorial Pro-Am on June 3. "That song was designed for one thing," he added. "To have fun and tell the world what I love to do and what I strive to do." Songwriters Chase McGill and Matt Dragstrem also shut down the false narrative during an interview with Rolling Stone. "[Bryan] is the least artificial person I’ve ever met," McGill said. "The only way I’ve actually succeeded in country music, ever, is by sitting in the room with good friends and enjoying making the song up that day. I don’t believe that I would feel any fulfillment from saying, ‘AI, write me a song about whatever.’ That’s not what I signed up for." The idea behind the song came up organically, said McGill. "Luke was texting one of his buddies, and the guy was like, ‘Let’s hang soon,’" he said. articles.title: Carmen Electra turns heads in barely-there look during breakfast while on her European vacation
articles.summary: Carmen Electra's bold Berlin breakfast photos on Instagram show the 54-year-old actress posing in lace underwear and micro shorts on her balcony.
articles.body: Carmen Electra chose a bold outfit to enjoy the most important meal of the day. In a recent Instagram post, the 54-year-old actress and model left little to the imagination when she shared photos from her "breakfast in berlin 🍓🍌." One of the photos shows the "Epic Movie" star standing near the breakfast table on her balcony in blue lingerie worn over it featuring adjustable drawstring ties hanging from each hip. She paired the look with a matching blue bra, which she cheekily pulled down in one photo and posed with slices of pineapples cleverly placed in front of her chest. CARMEN ELECTRA CHANNELS HER PLAYBOY PAST IN LEOPARD-PRINT BUNNY COSTUME ON THE RED CARPET In another photo, Electra is seen sitting down to eat in her bold breakfast attire, opting for various fruits, including berries, grapes, melons and Coca-Cola. "Still the most gorgeous ❤️❤️" one fan wrote in the comments section, while another added, "wtf🤔shes geting younger?🔥👍❤️" "Carm babes you look amazing!!!❤️🙌🔥" a third follower wrote and a fourth chimed in writing, "Whoa whoa whoa!! Breakfast for Champions 😎." Electra recently made her return to Playboy after she first appeared in the pages of the magazine in 1996 when she was 24. articles.title: Google needs Hollywood more than the studios need AI
articles.summary: Google has everything to gain from striking licensing deals with movie studios, but the entertainment industry has to be careful about how it embraces AI.
articles.body: Google has reportedly been reaching out to a number of Hollywood’s biggest studios, hoping to strike licensing agreements that would allow it to train its AI models on copyrighted material in exchange for massive piles of cash. In theory, these deals would be a win-win: a huge financial boon to the studios that would also give Google a significant advantage in its race to outpace other AI companies. But while there’s little downside for Google, these deals pose a distinct set of risks to each of the studios that might be thinking about going all-in on AI. Getting into bed with Google this way might benefit Hollywood in the short term, but it could just as easily backfire and leave the public feeling burned by the entertainment industry. Though Google has not yet been able to get Disney, Warner Bros. Discovery, or Universal to agree to anything officially, the company’s executives have been reaching out to multiple studio representatives with pitches focused on its AI technology, according to unnamed sources speaking to The Los Angeles Times. Google wants permission to train its AI models on the studios’ vast libraries of copyrighted content, and it’s willing to spend hundreds of millions of dollars to get ahold of them. Per The LA Times, Google could pay a studio like Disney / Pixar around $40 million just for the rights to generate outputs featuring a single copyrighted character. That payout could swell well into the billions the more characters Google’s deals encompass, and studios might be able to secure a portion of however much advertising revenue Google makes from AI-generated content featuring that IP on platforms like YouTube. As expensive as these partnerships would be for Google, they would also be an invaluable tool as the company continues to crystalize its position as one of the most prominent players in the AI game. Gemini being able to spit out Disney-approved images of Darth Vader and Snow White might not seem all that significant on its face, but that’s exactly the sort of thing that could get more ordinary, non tech-obsessed people seeing generative AI in a more positive (if innocuous) light. After years of hearing AI companies boast about their plans to disrupt society and eliminate jobs, public sentiment — especially among young people — about the technology has shifted into the negative. Even with tools like ChatGPT being as popular as they are, the larger AI industry has been so mired in controversy and plagued by concerns about its real world harms that it would now be hard-pressed to put out products that would immediately curry widespread goodwill. Striking deals with film and TV studios would give Google a convenient way to shift the larger narrative about its AI ambitions. The content developed through these partnerships would presumably look better than the slop currently being churned out by models trained on ill-gotten source data, and having Google’s name and logos slapped all over official AI-generated Disney content would do wonders to legitimize this technology in people’s minds. But even if it didn’t, the partnership would still signal to the public that the entertainment industry sees generative AI as a tool worth embracing. It’s hard to quantify how valuable that framing would be to Google, whose DeepMind arm struck a $75 million investment deal with A24 earlier this summer. But it’s very easy to imagine how taking Google’s AI cash could put studios on a path that ultimately alienates their workers and audiences. Regardless of whether a studio were to incorporate AI tools into their production workflows or simply feature user-generated AI content on their platforms (which was Disney and OpenAI’s plan before their partnership collapsed), striking a licensing agreement with Google would be a watershed moment. Lionsgate, a notable studio but not a major player, struck a licensing deal with Runway in 2024. So far, nothing concrete has come out of that partnership, but the companies say they’re working on a plan to release AI-generated shorts. Once any one of the big legacy studios hop on to the AI bandwagon and manage to actually make something they can show the world, more production houses have a reason to follow suit. AI’s potential to speed production timelines up while keeping costs down is one of the main things that has kept studios interested in utilizing the technology. Shareholders would absolutely love it if production houses could put out more movies while spending less money, but doing that by using AI tools would almost certainly put a significant portion of the entertainment workforce out of jobs. What may be keeping Disney and other studios from rushing to take Google up on its offers is the way that people have reacted to seeing AI used in the production of films like Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Fans were dismayed to find AI-generated images in Brand New Day’s official artbook, and the negative reaction might have been even more intense had people known about the technology’s use before the film hit theaters. It’s impossible to know for sure whether awareness about AI’s presence in Brand New Day’s production would have kept it from making $2 billion at the box office. But it stands to reason that none of the studios is eager to be the first to learn what happens when they release a project that’s presented as being the product of Google’s AI tools. Though Google has everything to gain from Hollywood embracing AI, the studios have to be mindful of how endorsing this technology could leave them out on a limb. And as much as Google might be presenting its products as the solution to all of the entertainment industry’s issues, the AI industry needs Hollywood more than Hollywood needs more slop.

articles.title: Jennifer Aniston’s boyfriend, Jim Curtis, reveals what 'Friends' star is really like behind closed doors
articles.summary: Wellness coach Jim Curtis opened up on a podcast about Jennifer Aniston's private, loving nature and the relationship tools the couple relies on.
articles.body: Jennifer Aniston’s boyfriend, Jim Curtis, is offering a rare glimpse into their relationship, from how they handle disagreements to what the actress is really like behind closed doors. Curtis, a wellness coach and author, opened up about his romance with the "Friends" star, revealing that their relationship is going strong. "It's going really well. My experience of her is so grounded and so open and caring and kind and loving," he gushed during a recent appearance on "The Jamie Kern Lima Show" podcast. JENNIFER ANISTON'S BOYFRIEND FLAUNTS STEAMY ROMANCE IN RARE PDA-PACKED PHOTOS The couple, who have been linked for more than a year, have largely kept their relationship private. But Curtis offered a candid look at their life together, including how they handle disagreements and what it means to be welcomed into Aniston’s close-knit inner circle. "She uses words like ‘my love.’ … She has this group of best friends that are like family," he said. "I feel incredibly blessed to be part and welcomed into that family, and I feel blessed to be in a relationship with someone that is so open-hearted." Curtis also praised Aniston for staying grounded despite her fame. JENNIFER ANISTON OFFERS RARE PEEK INTO HOLIDAY CELEBRATIONS WITH BOYFRIEND JIM CURTIS "Inclusive. Isn't that a beautiful thing? We're really a model for how we can all be in this world, right?" Curtis said. He said Aniston stands out because she stays true to herself despite her Hollywood fame. "She has an opportunity. Like, you would understand if she was less so. … Right? I think that she is a real example of stepping into possibility, as she came from ... living in New York and New Jersey, and, like, there was … this kind of household name and retained herself." Curtis also got candid about what happens when the couple disagrees. JASON ALDEAN SAYS HE AND WIFE BRITTANY ‘AGREE TO DISAGREE’ AFTER 11 YEARS OF MARRIAGE AS THEY TEAM UP FOR DUET The pair, he revealed, lean on relationship tools such as communication, acceptance and understanding instead of letting disagreements escalate. "We do a lot of meditation. We do a lot of talk," Curtis said. He explained that because the relationship is still relatively new, they don't necessarily need heavy resolution techniques. articles.title: Ed Sheeran concert workers hospitalized after forklift incident in Detroit: report
articles.summary: A forklift accident during Ed Sheeran's concert load-out at Ford Field in Detroit injured six workers after equipment reportedly "lost control" near a tunnel.
articles.body: Six people were injured Saturday during the load-out process after Ed Sheeran's concert at Ford Field in Detroit. The Detroit Fire Department responded to a "forklift injury accident" at the stadium around 11 p.m., according to Click On Detroit. Six workers were then transported to a local hospital. Several workers said they were headed on a break during their shift when the equipment "lost control" and hit "several of them" as the stage was being torn down near a vehicle tunnel, the outlet reported. LIONEL RICHIE HOSPITALIZED IN ST. LOUIS AFTER SUMMER OF HEALTH SCARES AND CANCELED CONCERTS One crew member was released from a hospital Sunday after an overnight stay. Another crew member who was hit in the chest told the outlet he'd "never experienced anything like that" and that everything "happened in a split second." KACEY MUSGRAVES ABRUPTLY CANCELS CONCERT DATES FROM 'MIDDLE OF NOWHERE' TOUR Of the individuals transported to hospitals, no injuries appeared to be life-threatening. During transportation, the outlet reported, two patients were in serious condition while the other four were in stable condition. "Ford Field has begun a full review and is cooperating with the appropriate authorities and with the event’s production partners," the stadium told the outlet. "Out of respect for the people involved and the integrity of that review, we will not speculate on the cause. We are grateful to the Detroit Fire Department and EMS for their rapid response." articles.title: Thea Frodin, who depicted Serena Williams as ‘King Richard’ body double, makes US Open debut
articles.summary: NEW YORK — Five years ago, Thea Frodin depicted Serena Williams in the Oscar-winning movie “King Richard,” performing as a body double. In a full-circle mome...
articles.body:
NEW YORK — Five years ago, Thea Frodin depicted Serena Williams in the Oscar-winning movie "King Richard," performing as a body double.

In a full-circle moment Tuesday afternoon, Frodin competed in a tournament that Williams long dominated.

Frodin, 17, made her WTA Tour debut in the first round of the US Open, losing to second-seeded Elena Rybakina 6-3, 6-2 at the Grandstand stadium.

Despite the final outcome, the California-born Frodin held her own in front of a supportive American crowd, ripping 11 aces and taking five games against the reigning Australian Open champion.

"I tried going out there to see what it would be like just to feel no pressure," Frodin said. "Yeah, just go out there and have a fun time. I feel like that's what I accomplished, and obviously I have a lot to learn, but I'm excited with most of the things I did out there."

A soon-to-be high school senior, Frodin earned a wild-card entry at the US Open by winning the USTA Billie Jean King Girls' 18s National Championships.

But long before then, Frodin cemented her place in mainstream culture by serving as the body double to actress Demi Singleton, who played a young Serena in the 2021 sports biopic about the Williams sisters' upbringing by their eccentric father, Richard Williams.

Will Smith starred as the title character and won Best Actor at the Academy Awards for his portrayal.

Frodin said she had not yet met Serena, who was an executive producer on the film. Serena — a six-time singles champion at the US Open — is set to compete with her sister Venus Williams in the doubles tournament at Flushing Meadows this week.

"Hopefully I can get the chance soon, to get the opportunity to meet her," said Frodin, who is No. 585 in the world rankings.

Frodin commanded more fanfare than the typical wild-card participant due to her Hollywood history. While Frodin certainly noticed the attention, she said it did not affect her.

"I think it's hard to get away from all of that," Frodin said. "It's kind of just about accepting it and not letting it get to you. I feel like I did a good job of that. Obviously, I saw that Will Smith reposted one of my posts, so that was pretty cool."

The Kazakhstan-born Rybakina said her team informed her of Frodin's unique backstory. She came away impressed by the teenager.

"I didn't see the movie," Rybakina, 27, said. "But yeah, it's a cool experience, definitely."
authors: Peter Sblendorio, New York Daily News
